items.project_definition: A synchronization gate validating that all prerequisites for a specific architectural layer are satisfied before dependent stories commence.
The shared infrastructure layer containing entity definitions and storage helpers that blocks all user-facing feature work.
The desired operational outcome for a specific user story, defining the primary value delivered to the end-user.
A unique sequential numeric value assigned to each item to enable targeted reference and mutation.
The standardized text-based data interchange format used for persistent storage in ~/.todos.json and machine-readable output.
The minimal set of functional capabilities, specifically focused on adding and completing items, required for initial validation.
The structural grouping of implementation tasks based on their alignment with specific user stories to ensure independent testability.
The set of design and contract documents required before any implementation logic is written.
The primary documentation file describing the usage and storage behavior of the command-line utility.
The initial phase involving package skeleton creation and tooling configuration via pyproject.toml.
The specific implementation task for providing user feedback when the task collection is empty.
The verification suite comprising unit and integration directory structures to validate the correctness of the service layer.
The automatic assignment of a timestamp to the created_at field during item instantiation.
The operation that removes all items marked as finished from the persistent storage.
The operation that retrieves and displays all stored items in either human-readable or machine-parseable formats.
A high-priority constraint indicating that no subsequent user story can begin until the associated phase is fully completed.
